predecessors.note: The march was originally part of a wider area 'established by King Berengar II about 950'; 'Otto appointed Aleramo margrave of the newly created March of Montferrat' (967). The land is the named-town core of the first keyframe, not the two provinces.

successors.note: 'the remainder passing to Savoy in 1708' (Montferrat page); Trino and Alba had gone to Savoy in 1631. The remainder is drawn as Casale and Nizza Monferrato, a minimum.

capitals.name: Chivasso
capitals.note: Page: 'The capital of Montferrat at this time was Chivasso' (13th-century context). The page gives no capital for other years; the span is the century.

capitals.name: Casale Monferrato
capitals.note: Casale page: in 1471 William VIII 'had chosen Casale as the permanent location of the marquisate court'; 'later became the capital of the marquessate' after 1292 (undated) and 'served as the capital of the House of Palaiologos'. No page names a capital for 1300-1470; Casale is outside the drawn shape in 1370-1403 (Visconti).

union.text: Chivasso, the 13th-century centre of the margraves' power

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, redrawn after review (the earlier shape was the whole Alessandria and Asti provinces). Area check: no page gives an area. The Montferrat page's 'It comprises roughly (and its extent has varied over time) the modern provinces of Alessandria and Asti' is written in the present tense and describes the region, not the state; the Marquisate page has Montferrat fighting 'the independence-minded communes of Asti and Alessandria', and the Alessandria page has Alessandria granted to Boniface of Montferrat as a fief in 1193 and its captaincy given to William VII, so the two cities were not simply Montferrat land, and Alessandria is Visconti land in the Lordship of Milan dossier from 1313 (and Cliopatria's Duchy of Milan 1402-1539). Reading chosen: named-town core. Chivasso (20 km) because the Marquisate page says 'The capital of Montferrat at this time was Chivasso, the centre of the margraves' power' (13th century); Trino (12 km) because the War of the Mantuan Succession page has it Montferrat's in 1628 (its acquisition is undated; Trino and Chivasso pages are silent). Early extent is confidence 1.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Casale page: 'It fell under the power of the Marquess of Montferrat in 1292' and 'later became the capital of the marquessate'. The 20 km circle stands for the town and 'the countryside near Casale Monferrato' of the Montferrat page; the radius is my reading.

New keyframe. The Chivasso circle is dropped at the dynasty change as a bridge (confidence 1): the Marquisate page says the Palaiologoi held Montferrat 'until 1533, during a period of diminishing territoriality' but names no loss, and no page opened dates Chivasso passing to another power.

correction.text: Trino, Casale, Asti, Mondovi, Chieri, Alba and Pavia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The war of 1356: Montferrat occupies Asti (23 January), 'also took Mondovi and Chieri from the Visconti', conquered Alba, and holds Pavia (imperial vicariate; 'Asti and Pavia remained to the Marquis of Montferrat' in 1358). Cuneo is not drawn: the page gives it both to Montferrat and, in June 1356, to Philip II of Taranto. Circles are my reading.

New keyframe. Peace of 8 June 1358: 'Novara and Alba returned to the Visconti, while Asti and Pavia remained with the Marquis of Montferrat'. Mondovi and Chieri are dropped as a bridge: the page does not say what happened to them (confidence 1).
New keyframe. Visconti of Milan page: 'In 1359, Pavia surrendered to Galeazzo II'.
New keyframe. Casale page: Casale was 'conquered by the Visconti of Milan in 1370' and 'remained under their control until 1404'.

New keyframe. Asti page: 'John ruled over Asti until 1372'. Only Trino remains in the drawn core; Montferrat's other holdings in these decades are on no page opened (confidence 1; the shape is a minimum).

New keyframe. Casale returns after the Visconti control that lasted 'until 1404'; the Casale page has William VIII choosing Casale as the permanent court in 1471. The Palaiologan holdings (Acqui, Moncalvo, Valenza and others) are on no page opened. Held 1533-1536 under Spanish occupation (own events).

correction.text: Trino, Casale, Alba and Nizza Monferrato

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, redrawn. Alba and Nizza Monferrato are added as a bridge (confidence 1): the War of the Mantuan Succession page has Montferrat holding Trino, Nizza and Alba in 1628-1631 ('Savoyard forces captured Trino in April, then Nizza Monferrato in June'; the infobox has 'Savoy annexes Trino and Alba'), and the Alba page says only that 'Montferrat and the Visconti fought over the town; later it became a possession of the Gonzaga' (undated). The Casale page: 'In 1536 it passed to the Gonzagas of Mantua'.

New keyframe. 'With the War of the Mantuan Succession (1628-1631) a piece of the duchy passed to the Duchy of Savoy' (Montferrat page); the War page names Trino and Alba. What remained was the Gonzaga duchy at Casale; the pages name no other town, so this shape is a minimum (soft).

ledger.note: 967: Otto I creates the March of Montferrat for Aleramo. 'Otto appointed Aleramo margrave of the newly created March of Montferrat' (the infobox says 967-1574; the Montferrat page says elevated to a margravate in 961). The land is my reading: Chivasso (the 13th-century seat) and Trino; the Montferrat page's 'provinces of Alessandria and Asti' describes the region, not the state (see the first keyframe).

1292: Casale falls to the Marquess of Montferrat. Casale page: 'It fell under the power of the Marquess of Montferrat in 1292' and 'later became the capital of the marquessate'. The 20 km circle (town and countryside) is my reading. The Matteo I Visconti page has Matteo 'taking Casale' in 1292 after the death of William VII; the two pages are not reconciled.
1305: the Aleramici die out and the Palaiologos dynasty inherits. 'In 1305, the last Aleramici margrave died'; the Palaiologoi 'held it until 1533'. Dynasty change; colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Chivasso, the 13th-century centre of the margraves' power

ledger.note: 1305: the Chivasso circle is dropped as a bridge (confidence 1). The Marquisate page says the Palaiologoi 'held it until 1533, during a period of diminishing territoriality' but names no town; the Chivasso page is silent on Montferrat. A gap-filler should date Chivasso's passing to another power.

1356: Montferrat takes Alba, Mondovi and Chieri from the Visconti. Lordship of Milan page: 'the Marquis of Montferrat also conquered Alba, Cuneo, and also took Mondovi and Chieri from the Visconti'. Cuneo is not booked here: the same page has Philip II of Taranto acquiring 'Mondovi, Morozzo, Cuneo and Cherasco' in June 1356, so it goes to him in the Milan dossier. Mirrors lordship-of-milan.

1356: Pavia passes to Montferrat's side. The Lordship of Milan page has Galeazzo besieging Pavia in April 1356 and the Marquis holding the imperial vicariate of Pavia; after the peace 'Asti and Pavia remained to the Marquis of Montferrat'. The page does not say when Pavia left Visconti hands, so the year is a floor (confidence 2). Mirrors lordship-of-milan.

23 January 1356: Montferrat occupies Asti. Asti page: 'John II expanded the territory of Montferrat and ultimately in 1356 took Asti from the Visconti', 'ending 16 years of control by Milan'; the Lordship of Milan page has the war beginning 'on 23 January 1356 with the occupation of Asti'. Mirrors lordship-of-milan.
8 June 1358: Alba returns to the Visconti. Lordship of Milan page: the peace signed 'on 8 June 1358 in Milan in Sant'Ambrogio'; 'Novara and Alba returned to the Visconti'. Mirrors lordship-of-milan.

8 June 1358: Mondovi and Chieri are dropped as a bridge (confidence 1). The peace lists what Montferrat kept (Asti, Pavia) and what returned (Novara, Alba); the page does not say what happened to Chieri or Mondovi, and gives Mondovi to Philip II of Taranto in June 1356.

1359: Pavia goes to Galeazzo II. Visconti of Milan page: 'In 1359, Pavia surrendered to Galeazzo II.' The page does not say the surrender was to Montferrat's side, so the counterpart is the new holder. Mirrors lordship-of-milan.
1370: the Visconti conquer Casale. Casale page: 'conquered by the Visconti of Milan in 1370' and 'it remained under their control until 1404'. Mirrors lordship-of-milan.
1372: Montferrat loses Asti. Asti page: 'John ruled over Asti until 1372'; the city then governs itself and 'seven years later' submits to the Visconti (see lordship-of-milan).

1404: Casale returns to Montferrat. Casale page: the Visconti held it 'until 1404'; in 1471 William VIII 'had chosen Casale as the permanent location of the marquisate court'. The page does not say who gave it up; the Duchy of Milan held the Visconti lands.
1533: Charles V seizes Montferrat. 'Montferrat was seized by the Spanish under Emperor Charles V of Habsburg.'

1536: Charles V gives Montferrat to Federico II Gonzaga. He 'restored it to Federico II, Duke of Mantua from the House of Gonzaga in 1536' (the Duchy of Mantua page says Mantua acquired Montferrat in 1531 by the marriage of Federico and Margaret Palaiologina).

1536: the Gonzaga dukes of Mantua rule Montferrat. The Montferrat page: the territory 'passed to the Gonzaga Dukes of Mantua (1536-1708)'. A personal union: Montferrat keeps its own dossier and is drawn as the Mantuan vassal.

1536: Alba and Nizza Monferrato are shown as Montferrat's from the Gonzaga union, as a bridge (confidence 1). Alba page: 'Montferrat and the Visconti fought over the town; later it became a possession of the Gonzaga' (undated); the War of the Mantuan Succession page has Montferrat holding both in 1628. No page dates either acquisition.

1536: Montferrat is ruled by the Gonzaga dukes of Mantua as a personal union, drawn as the Mantuan vassal. Marquisate page: Charles V 'restored it to Federico II, Duke of Mantua from the House of Gonzaga in 1536'; the Montferrat page: 'passed to the Gonzaga Dukes of Mantua (1536-1708)'. Mirrors duchy-of-mantua /ledger/3 (whose region is still the older two-province shape).
1574: Montferrat becomes a duchy. 'In 1574, Montferrat was raised to a Duchy by Maximilian II, Holy Roman Emperor.'
March 1628: the Spanish begin the siege of Casale. 'Siege operations only began in March' (Casale, 1628); the siege 'resumed in June' 1629 with a French garrison of 2,500.
April 1628: Savoy takes Trino. 'Led by Charles Emmanuel, Savoyard forces captured Trino in April, then Nizza Monferrato in June.'
29 October 1630: the Spanish withdraw from Casale. 'the Spanish finally withdrew' on 29 October; the page's context gives 1630.

19 June 1631: the Treaty of Cherasco confirms Nevers as Duke of Montferrat and gives Savoy Trino and Alba. Infobox: 'Savoy annexes Trino and Alba'; the main text says only 'in return for minor concessions to Savoy'.
19 June 1631: the war ends with the Treaty of Cherasco, 'which confirmed Nevers as Duke of Mantua and Montferrat'.

1708: the Gonzaga union ends with the last Gonzaga duke. Montferrat page: 'the remainder passing to Savoy in 1708, as Leopold I, Holy Roman Emperor gained possession of the Gonzaga territory'. Mirrors duchy-of-mantua /ledger/6.
1708: Montferrat passes to Savoy. 'the remainder passing to Savoy in 1708', as 'Leopold I gained the Gonzaga territory'.
1708: the Duchy of Montferrat ends with the Gonzaga line; its remainder goes to Savoy.

wars.name: War of the Mantuan Succession
wars.outcome: Spain besieged Casale (1628-1630) and Savoy took Trino and Nizza Monferrato; the Treaty of Cherasco (19 June 1631) confirmed Nevers as Duke of Mantua and Montferrat, with Savoy keeping Trino and Alba and French garrisons staying in Casale and Pinerolo.

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundaries or an area. The state is drawn as circles at the towns the pages name (Chivasso, Trino, Casale, Asti, Pavia, Alba, Mondovi, Chieri, Nizza), not as the modern provinces of Alessandria and Asti, which the Montferrat page gives as the extent of the region.

notes: Written from three pages and repaired 2026-10-31 after review (verdict fail) from nine more. The review found the whole Alessandria and Asti provinces drawn for 967-1708, which is the region the Montferrat page describes, not the state, and which overlapped the Lordship of Milan (Alessandria from 1313) and Cliopatria's Duchy of Milan 1402-1539. Reading chosen: the state is drawn as circles at the towns the pages name (Chivasso, Trino, Casale, Asti, Pavia, Alba, Mondovi, Chieri, Nizza Monferrato), with dated gains and losses where a page dates them (Casale 1292, 1370, 1404; the war of 1356-1358; Asti 1356-1372; Pavia 1356-1359); the Lordship of Milan dossier subtracts the same circles from its Alessandria and Vercelli provinces, so the two do not overlap. Everything between the dated points is a minimum, confidence 1. Not settled: when Trino, Alba and Nizza Monferrato came to Montferrat (first attested 1628; Alba and Nizza are bridged in at 1536); when Chivasso left Montferrat (bridged out at 1305, the dynasty change); the Palaiologan holdings (Acqui, Moncalvo, Valenza, Ivrea and others) are on no page opened, so the 1305-1533 and 1631-1708 shapes are minima; the 1345 division of the Angevin possessions between Montferrat and Milan (Alessandria page) names no place; Novara 'returned to the Visconti' in 1358 but no page says who held it (not drawn); capitals 1300-1470; the Casale page has Casale to Montferrat in 1292 while the Matteo I Visconti page has Matteo 'taking Casale' that year; the Mantua page says Mantua got Montferrat in 1531, the Montferrat page 1536 (Spanish seizure 1533-1536). The 1536 and 1708 vassal events now mirror duchy-of-mantua /ledger/3 and /ledger/6, but those two Mantua events still carry the older Alessandria and Asti province shape and need the new region. House-of-savoy /ledger/11 and /ledger/20 name duchy-of-mantua rather than this state as the loser of Trino, Alba and the 1708 remainder. Counterparts without dossiers: Commune of Casale, Commune of Asti. No gazetteer names needed.
